To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and tested an efficient BCI interface for object selection using the P300 oddball paradigm.

a) a novel vision based BCI for grasping an object using a robotic arm was designed, b) a novel dynamically sized non-universal grid stimulus was designed to improve the efficiency of the system, c) an average accuracy of 86.5% was achieved for stimulus selection and d) the system took an average of 6 commands for the user to perform an action on an object.
a novel vision based P300 BCI system has been designed, implemented, and tested for selecting an object and grasping it via a wheelchair-mounted robotic system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a BCI system to assist paralyzed patients in their daily life, in particular, in performing ADL tasks.
the development of a vision based Brain Computer Interface for selecting an object in the environment and then grasping that object using a robotic arm.
the design of a BCI based interface for controlling a WMRA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system presented here is a novel and effective vision-based BCI for selecting and manipulating objects in the environment.
the proposed vision based BCI system for grasping using the WMRA is a promising system for ADL tasks.

the proposed system is an efficient and robust system that allows a user to perform complete ADL tasks using BCI, and a robotic arm mounted on a wheelchair, without losing concentration or attention on the stimuli or task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a vision based P300 BCI was developed to perform a complete ADL task using a WMRA, which is the first of its kind.
we developed a novel vision based P300 BCI for selecting an object and grasping it with a WMRA.
we have successfully designed, developed, and tested a system that uses a BCI and a wheelchair-mounted robotic system to perform ADL tasks for paralyzed patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed system can be used to perform complete ADL tasks using the BCI, and the WMRA.
